sentences.text: Researchers developed a gelatin-based hydrogel designed to encapsulate vesicles derived from stem cells cultured in a three-dimensional structure.
In a mouse model of brain injury, this delivery system was injected into the damaged region, with recovery assessed through behavioral tests, cell staining, and gene analysis.
The gel remained in the brain longer than controls, resulted in less tissue damage, and was associated with improved movement and memory over time.

The treatment increased the number of dividing cells showing markers for nerve cells or their support cells, a process linked to elevated protein levels that triggered gene changes supporting new nerve cell growth.
